page: Amazon Web Services c7a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processors. Operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, this instance provisions 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 96.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB per core. The platform supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as cryptographic accelerations such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance exhibits top-tier multi-threaded compute capabilities, scoring in the top 10 percent for stress-ng multi-core tests and Geekbench multi-core evaluation. Software compilation performance under Clang reached 65,336.0, reflecting parallel efficiency across all 48 dedicated physical execution units. Memory throughput is supported by DDR5 architecture, with uncached large-block reads measuring 226.53 GB/sec and writes reaching 131.26 GB/sec. Benchmark results also demonstrate 113.42 million Redis SET operations per second and 45.31 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The instance includes a baseline network throughput of 19 Gbps but bundles neither local NVMe storage nor discrete GPUs. As an architectural tradeoff, persistence relies entirely on network-attached storage. The 1:2 memory-to-core ratio yields resource density aligned strictly with CPU-bound processing rather than memory-heavy database workloads. Dedicated single-threaded cores eliminate hyperthreading contention, maximizing execution efficiency for distributed batch processing, CI/CD build infrastructure, scientific modeling, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro System and powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Utilizing dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it couples 96.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory at a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The architecture provides 19 Gbps of baseline networking and features hardware-level AVX-512 vector extensions. In synthetic benchmarks, it ranks in the top 10 percent for multi-core stress testing and Clang compilation speed, supported by an uncached read memory bandwidth of 226.53 GB/sec. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. This hardware profile provides cost-effective throughput for compute-intensive workloads that require predictable multi-core execution, including large software compilation pipelines, batch processing engines, vector-accelerated scientific simulations, and CPU-based inference deployments.
